Aggregator directories (datacenterHawk, DataCenterMap) give 1 Superloop Circle, Reno, NV as the address for this campus, the same address appears attached to more than one individually numbered Tahoe Reno building on these directories, so it is treated here as a shared campus level address rather than a distinct address for any one building. Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator. The same press release specifically names TAHOE RENO 1 as the campus first building, describing it as up to 1.3 million square feet and up to 130 MW of power capacity, a tier-1 operator figure for this specific building, given as an up to design target rather than a confirmed current operating figure, so also not applied to critical_it_mw.

reading.body:
Tahoe Reno 1 is the first building of Switch's Citadel Campus, a 2,000-acre site in Storey County designed for up to 650 MW of total power across multiple buildings at full buildout. The operator specifies Tahoe Reno 1 itself as a design target of up to 1.3 million square feet and up to 130 MW of power capacity, but publishes no confirmed operating figure for this building, so its current state is not known from published sources.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities but only two publish power specifications, for a combined total of 10.37 MW. Tahoe Reno 1 ranks third in the state by published megawatts, a rank that reflects the absence of published figures from most other sites rather than confirmation of its own operating capacity.

The campus sits adjacent to Tesla's Gigafactory in an industrial park designed for large-scale infrastructure. No certifications, grid connections, cooling systems, or current tenant commitments are published for this facility. Whether Tahoe Reno 1 matters to AI scaling depends on whether the operator achieves the stated 130 MW target and whether the parent grid can supply it, neither of which is yet confirmed in available sources.
